title: Aesop's Fables
author: Aesop
ru: Десять знаменитых басен о животных и людях — короткие истории с моралью.

chapters.title: Fable 1. The Fox and the Grapes
chapters.text:
It is a hot day in summer. A fox is walking on a road. He is very hungry and very thirsty. He has no food, and there is no water near him.

Then the fox sees a garden. In the garden there is a big vine. On the vine there are grapes. They are big, dark and sweet. The fox looks at them.

“Oh, those grapes are beautiful!” he says. “They are just right for a hot day. I want them!”

But the grapes are high on the vine. The fox runs and jumps. He can't reach them. He goes back, runs again, and jumps higher. No! He can't reach them. He tries again and again. He jumps ten times. He is tired now, and his legs hurt.

The fox sits down and looks up at the grapes. Then he stands up. He puts his nose in the air and walks away.

“I don't want those grapes,” he says. “They are not ripe. I am sure they are sour. Sour grapes are bad for me.”

A little bird is sitting in a tree. It is watching the fox, and it is laughing.

Moral: Some people say that a thing is bad when they can't have it.

chapters.title: Fable 2. The Tortoise and the Hare
chapters.text:
A hare lives in a green field. He can run very fast, and he is very proud. Every day he laughs at the other animals.

One day the hare sees a tortoise. The tortoise is walking very, very slowly.

“Ha! Look at you!” says the hare. “You are so slow. Are you walking or sleeping?”

The tortoise looks at him. “Yes, I am slow,” she says. “But I can win a race with you.”

The hare laughs and laughs. “You? Win a race with me? Fine! Let's race!”

All the animals come to watch. The fox is the judge. “Ready, steady, go!” he says.

The hare runs very fast. Soon he can't see the tortoise. He stops under a big tree.

“The tortoise is so slow,” he thinks. “I have a lot of time. I can sleep a little.”

He lies down and closes his eyes. Soon he is sleeping.

The tortoise doesn't stop. She walks and walks, slowly but all the time. She walks past the tree and the sleeping hare.

Later, the hare wakes up. He looks around. Where is the tortoise? He runs to the end of the race. But the tortoise is there! She is the winner. All the animals are cheering.

Moral: Slow and steady wins the race.

chapters.title: Fable 3. The Lion and the Mouse
chapters.text:
A big lion is sleeping in the forest. A little mouse is running around. She doesn't see the lion, and she runs over his nose.

The lion wakes up. He is angry. He puts his big paw on the mouse.

“Now I am going to eat you!” he says.

“Oh, please, King of the Animals!” says the mouse. “Please let me go. I am very small. I am not a good dinner for you. And one day I can help you.”

The lion laughs. “You? Help me? You are so small, and I am the king!” But the lion is not hungry, and he thinks the mouse is funny. He lifts his paw. The mouse runs away.

A few days later, some hunters come to the forest. They put a big net on the ground. The lion walks into it. Now he can't move. He is roaring and roaring.

The little mouse hears him too. She runs to the lion.

“Don't worry,” she says. “I can help you.”

She starts to bite the ropes of the net with her little teeth. Soon there is a big hole in the net. The lion is free!

“Thank you, little friend,” says the lion. “You are small, but you are a very good friend.”

Moral: Little friends can be great friends.

chapters.title: Fable 4. The Ant and the Grasshopper
chapters.text:
It is summer. The sun is shining, and the fields are green. A grasshopper is sitting on a leaf. He is singing and playing his violin. He is very happy.

An ant is walking past. She is carrying a big grain of corn. The grain is very heavy. She is working hard.

“Hello, Ant!” says the grasshopper. “Why are you working? It is a beautiful day. Come and sing with me!”

“I can't,” says the ant. “I am getting food for the winter. You can get food for the winter too.”

“Winter?” laughs the grasshopper. “Winter is far away. There is a lot of food now. I want to sing and dance.”

The ant goes on working. Every day she carries food to her home. Every day the grasshopper sings.

Then winter comes. It is very cold. There is snow on the fields. There is no food anywhere. The grasshopper is cold and very hungry. He walks to the ant's house and knocks on the door.

“Please, Ant,” he says. “I have no food. Can you give me some corn?”

“What are you doing all summer?” asks the ant.

“I am singing all day,” says the grasshopper.

“Singing all summer?” says the ant. “Then you can dance all winter!”

Moral: Work today, and you can eat tomorrow.

chapters.title: Fable 5. The Boy Who Cried Wolf
chapters.text:
A young boy lives in a small village near a big forest. His job is to watch the sheep on the hill. Every day he sits on the hill with the sheep. The work is very boring.

One day the boy has an idea. He runs down the hill and shouts, “Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is eating the sheep!”

The people of the village hear him. They stop their work and run up the hill. But there is no wolf. The boy is laughing.

“Ha ha! There is no wolf!” he says. “It is a joke!”

The people are angry. “Don't do that again,” they say, and they go home.

A few days later, the boy is bored again. “Wolf! Wolf!” he shouts. The people run up the hill again. Again there is no wolf. The people are very angry now.

The next evening, a real wolf comes out of the forest. It is big and grey. It is running to the sheep! The boy is very afraid.

“Wolf! Wolf!” he shouts. “Please help me! There is a wolf!”

The people in the village hear him. But they don't come. “He is joking again,” they say. “We don't believe him.”

The wolf eats many sheep.

Moral: Nobody believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth.

chapters.title: Fable 6. The Crow and the Pitcher
chapters.text:
It is a very hot summer. There is no rain. The rivers are dry. A crow is flying over the fields. She is very, very thirsty.

At last she sees a pitcher in a garden. She flies down to it. Yes, there is some water in the pitcher! But there is only a little water, at the bottom. The pitcher is tall, and its neck is narrow. The crow puts her beak in the pitcher, but she can't reach the water.

She tries to push the pitcher. She wants to turn it over. But the pitcher is too heavy for her.

The crow is sad. “What can I do?” she thinks. “I need water.”

Then she looks at the ground. There are many small stones there. The crow has an idea. She takes a stone in her beak and drops it into the pitcher. Then she takes another stone and drops it in. Then another, and another.

With every stone, the water is getting higher. The crow works for a long time. She is tired, but she doesn't stop. At last, the water is at the top of the pitcher. Now the crow can drink! She drinks and drinks. The water is cool and good.

Moral: When you really need something, you can find a way.

chapters.title: Fable 7. The Fox and the Crow
chapters.text:
A crow is sitting in a tree. She has a big piece of cheese in her beak. She is very happy. She wants to eat it.

A fox is walking under the tree. He sees the crow. He sees the cheese too. He is hungry, and he wants that cheese.

“How can I get it?” he thinks. Then he smiles. He has an idea.

“Good morning, beautiful bird!” he says. “Oh, how lovely you are today! Your feathers are so black and shiny. Your eyes are so bright. You are the most beautiful bird in the forest.”

The crow listens. She is very happy.

“And I am sure your voice is beautiful too,” says the fox. “Please sing for me. Just one song! Then I can call you the Queen of the Birds.”

The crow wants to be the Queen of the Birds. She opens her beak and sings, “Caw! Caw! Caw!”

The cheese falls down from her beak. The fox catches it and eats it quickly.

“Thank you,” says the fox. “You have a voice, yes. But you don't have a brain.”

And the fox walks away, happy and full.

Moral: Be careful of people who say too many nice things.

chapters.title: Fable 8. The North Wind and the Sun
chapters.text:
The North Wind and the Sun are talking in the sky. They are having an argument.

“I am stronger than you,” says the North Wind.

“No, I am stronger,” says the Sun.

Then they see a man. He is walking on a road. He is wearing a warm coat.

“Let's have a competition,” says the Sun. “Can you take the coat from that man? The winner is stronger.”

“Easy!” says the North Wind. “I can do it. Watch me!”

The North Wind starts to blow. He blows hard. The trees are moving, and the leaves are flying. But the man is holding his coat. The North Wind blows harder and harder. It is very cold now. The man is holding his coat very tightly. He doesn't want to lose it. At last the North Wind is tired. He stops.

“Now it is my turn,” says the Sun.

The Sun comes out from behind a cloud. He shines on the man, softly and warmly. The man is getting warm. He opens his coat. The Sun shines more. It is very hot now. The man takes off his coat. He sits down under a tree and puts his coat on the grass.

“You see?” says the Sun. “I am the winner.”

Moral: Kindness is often stronger than force.

chapters.title: Fable 9. The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
chapters.text:
A little mouse lives in the country. One day his cousin from the town comes to visit him.

The country mouse is very happy. He gives his cousin his best food: some corn, some beans and a little piece of bread.

The town mouse eats a little. He doesn't like it. “Cousin, how can you live here?” he says. “Your food is so simple. Your life is so boring. Come to the town with me. I have wonderful food there!”

So the two mice go to the town. The town mouse lives in a big house. In the dining room, there is a big table. On the table, there is cake, cheese, meat and fruit.

“Eat, eat!” says the town mouse. The country mouse is very happy.

Then the door opens. People are coming in! The two mice run and hide. They wait. Then they come back to the table. But now a big cat is coming! And then two big dogs! The mice run and hide again. The country mouse is shaking.

“Goodbye, cousin,” he says. “Your food is wonderful, but I am always afraid here. I am going home. My food is simple, but my life is quiet.”

Moral: A simple life in peace is better than a rich life in fear.

chapters.title: Fable 10. The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs
chapters.text:
A man and his wife live on a small farm. They are not rich. They have some chickens, a cow and one goose.

One morning, the man goes to the goose's nest. There is an egg in the nest. But it is not a white egg. It is yellow, and it is very heavy. It is gold!

“Look!” he says to his wife. “A golden egg!”

The next morning, there is another golden egg. And the next morning, another one. Every day the goose gives them one golden egg. They sell the eggs in the town. Soon they have a lot of money. They buy a big house, nice clothes and good food.

But the man and his wife want more. “One egg every day is too slow,” says the man. “We want to be very rich now.”

“I have an idea,” says his wife. “The goose has a lot of gold inside her. Let's open her and take all the gold today!”

So they kill the goose. They open her. But there is no gold inside. She is just a normal goose.

Now they have no golden eggs, and they have no goose. The man and his wife sit down and cry.

Moral: If you want too much, you can lose everything.
